intro: You have come to Seleucia, the ancient city at Silifke in Mersin province. Its story stretches from the 3rd century BC to the 13th century AD. Here a Temple of Zeus, a theatre and a medieval castle await you.
history: The city was founded by Seleucus I Nicator and grew on the banks of the Göksu, the ancient Calycadnus river. It stood at the crossroads of inland routes, and in Roman and Byzantine times that position made it an important centre of Cilicia.
structure-3: Look up at the hill above Silifke. Silifke Castle crowns it, a fortress whose story spans Byzantine to Karamanid times.
structure-4: You are now at the Roman Bridge. These are the remains of a stone bridge built in the Roman period. Imagine the travellers and carts that crossed here on their way inland.
structure-5: These are the Wall Remains, surviving sections of the defensive walls that once ran around the city.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Zeus and the Theatre.
facts: Did you know? Founded in the 3rd century BC, the city bears the name of the Seleucid dynasty: 'Seleucia on the Calycadnus'. Its founder, Seleucus I Nicator, was Alexander's general, and this is one of the many cities he named after himself. Here in 1190, on the Third Crusade, Frederick Barbarossa drowned in the Göksu — the ancient Calycadnus — and the crusade fell apart. Today a column of the Temple of Zeus and the Roman bridge still stand amid the traffic of modern Silifke.
outro: This brings our journey through Seleucia to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these stones keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
